title: Flip Three Neighbours to All Ones
statement:
You get an array nums of 0s and 1s. One operation picks three consecutive positions and flips all three (0 becomes 1, 1 becomes 0).

Return the fewest operations that turn every element into 1, or -1 if it cannot be done.

examples.why: Flip positions 0–2 to get [1, 1, 0, 0, 0, 1], then positions 2–4 to get all ones.
Only two zeros, yet one flip cannot fix both: flip 0–2 gives [1, 0, 0, 0], then flip 1–3.
The only possible flip covers all three positions, which turns [1, 0, 1] into [0, 1, 0]. Neither state is all ones.

hints: Flipping the same three positions twice changes nothing, and the order of flips does not matter. So each window is either flipped once or not at all.
Look at the leftmost position. Only one window can still change it once you have decided everything to its left. Is that choice forced?
Scan left to right. If nums[i] is 0, you must flip i..i+2 now. At the end, the last two positions must already be 1.

explain.intuition:
Two facts make this easy. Flips commute, so the order does not matter. And flipping a window twice cancels out, so each window is used zero or one time.

Now look at position 0. The only window that touches it is 0–2, so if nums[0] is 0 you are forced to flip it, and if it is 1 you are forced not to. After that decision, position 1 is touched only by window 1–3 among the remaining ones, and so on. Every choice is forced, so the greedy scan finds the only possible answer, and therefore the smallest. The last two positions have no window of their own; if either is still 0, the answer is -1.
steps: Copy the array (or flip in place) and set ops = 0.
For i from 0 to n − 3: if nums[i] is 0, flip nums[i], nums[i+1], nums[i+2] and add 1 to ops.
After the loop, if nums[n−2] or nums[n−1] is 0, return -1.
pitfalls: Counting zeros and dividing by three. Flips also turn 1s into 0s, as in [0, 1, 1, 0].
Forgetting to check the last two positions. The loop never fixes them directly, so they must come out as 1 on their own.
Flipping only nums[i] and forgetting the other two positions of the window.

complexity.space: O(1) extra if flipping in place

solutions.title: Try every set of windows
solutions.idea: Each window is flipped zero or one time. Try all 2^(n−2) choices and keep the smallest one that leaves all ones.

solutions.title: Forced greedy scan
solutions.idea: The leftmost 0 can only be fixed by the window that starts at it, so flip it there and move on.

followups: The window size is k instead of 3, and n is large. How do you avoid touching k elements per flip? (Hint: track how many active flips cover the current position.)
An operation flips a position and everything to its right. How does the greedy change?
